html:
Marco Polo was a merchant of Venice who spent about seventeen years in the China of Kublai Khan. Kinsay is his name for Hangzhou, capital of the Southern Song until the Mongols took it in 1276. He says he follows a report that the Song queen sent to the Mongol general, and that he later saw the city himself. His numbers are far too large.

First and foremost, then, the document stated the city of Kinsay to be so great that it hath an hundred miles of compass. And there are in it twelve thousand bridges of stone, for the most part so lofty that a great fleet could pass beneath them. And let no man marvel that there are so many bridges, for you see the whole city stands as it were in the water and surrounded by water, so that a great many bridges are required to give free passage about it.
Inside the city there is a Lake which has a compass of some 30 miles: and all round it are erected beautiful palaces and mansions, of the richest and most exquisite structure that you can imagine, belonging to the nobles of the city. There are also on its shores many abbeys and churches of the Idolaters. In the middle of the Lake are two Islands, on each of which stands a rich, beautiful and spacious edifice, furnished in such style as to seem fit for the palace of an Emperor.
The people are Idolaters; and since they were conquered by the Great Kaan they use paper-money.
